key_insight: The paper derives a principled, high-dimensional characterization of how large pretrained representations should be for best downstream linear-probing performance, showing there is an optimal representation size that depends on data statistics and label sample budget.
problem_solved: It addresses the practical and theoretical question of how to choose the dimensionality of pretrained features (representation size) to maximize generalization when adapting to new tasks with limited labeled data.
method: Formalize pretraining as structure extraction (principal components / low-rank signal + noise) in a high-dimensional asymptotic regime.
Derive closed-form/asymptotic expressions for downstream linear-probe risk as a function of representation dimension, sample sizes, noise & eigenvalue spectrum.
Use the analytic formulae to identify the representation size that minimizes downstream error and study trade-offs (under- vs over-parameterization, sample complexity).
impact: Provides actionable, theory-backed guidance for selecting representation dimensionality in transfer learning pipelines, helping practitioners balance pretraining cost and downstream performance when labeled data are scarce.
visual_elements: Schematic pipeline: large unlabelled pretraining -> bottleneck representation -> linear probe on small labelled set (icons + arrows).
Curve: downstream test error vs representation size showing a U-shaped behavior with a clear optimal point.
Heatmap / contour: optimal representation size as a function of labeled sample count and signal-to-noise (or eigenvalue decay).
Equation box: compact asymptotic formula (annotated) linking risk to representation dimension, samples, and spectrum.
paper_title: Optimal Representation Size: High-Dimensional Analysis of Pretraining and Linear Probing
paper_authors: Valentina Njaradi, Clémentine Dominé, Rachel Swanson, Marco Mondelli, Andrew Saxe
